title: Does a colour link nest with bold and code, and can it cross a line break?
body:
Agents colour text with a `color:` link, as in `[failed](color:red)` (7a387c5). Nobody has tried it around bold or inline code, as in `[**failed**](color:red)`, or on a span that cmr wraps onto a second row.

## Options

- Try each case against the renderer and record what it does. If the result reads well, the output style can allow it.
- Have the output style allow only plain words inside a colour link.

Lean: try it, since it takes one scenario and a look at the screen.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/bd10c4a0
notes.text: Jack, 2026-11-10: try each case against the renderer and record the result here. A case that draws badly gets fixed in coax.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/bd10c4a0
notes.text:
Tried each case through `markdown` in `src/ui.rs`, on `dev` at 4dcd056.

- `[**failed**](color:red)` draws `**failed**` in red. The asterisks show and nothing is bold.
- ``[`code`](color:red)`` draws `` `code` `` in red. The backticks show and there is no code style.
- `**[failed](color:red)**` draws `[failed](color:red)` in bold. The link markup shows and there is no colour.
- A colour span that wraps at width 14 stays red on every row. The spaces between its words carry no style, which makes no visible difference for a colour.

The first three come from cmr. `Inline::Link` keeps its text as a plain string, and so does `Inline::Bold` with its body. `inlines` in `../cmr/src/lib.rs` therefore never parses markup inside either one. coax cannot nest them without a change in cmr.

Both options on this issue still fit. cmr could parse inlines inside link text and inside bold. Or the output style could allow only plain words inside a colour link.
